content.paragraph: This discussion motivates the following definition.

note.title: Infinite Sequence
note.paragraph: An infinite sequence , denoted by $$\left\{ a_{n} \right\}$$ , is a function whose domain is the set of positive integers. The functional values $$a_{1},a_{2},a_{3},\ldots,a_{n}\text{,}\ldots$$ are the terms of the sequence, and the term $$a_{n}$$ is called the $$\mathbf{n}$$ th term of the sequence.

item.paragraph: The sequence $$\left\{ a_{n} \right\}$$ is also denoted by $$\left\{ a_{n} \right\}_{n = 1}^{\infty}$$ .

Sometimes it is convenient to begin a sequence with $$a_{k}$$ . In this case, the sequence is $$\left\{ a_{n} \right\}_{n = k}^{\infty}$$ , and its terms are $${a_{k},a_{k + 1},a_{k + 2},\ldots,a_{n}}\ldots$$

note.title: Note
note.paragraph: Notice that the function $$f{(n)} = n + 1$$ defining the sequence $$\left\{ n + 1 \right\}$$ may be viewed as the function $$f{(x)} = x + 1( - \infty < x < \infty)$$ with $$x$$ restricted to the set of positive integers. Similarly, the function defining the sequence $$\left\{ (n + 1) \slash n \right\}$$ is just the function $$f{(x)} = (x + 1) \slash x$$ with a similar restriction on its domain. Finally, the function defining the sequence $$\left\{ {( - 1)}^{n} \right\}$$ can be viewed as the function $$f{(x)} = \cos\pi x$$ with $$x$$ restricted to the set of positive integers.* These observations suggest that it is possible to study the properties of a sequence by analyzing the properties of a corresponding function defined for all values of $$x$$ in some suitable domain of $$f$$ .

subsection.title: The Limit of a Sequence
subsection.paragraph: Given a sequence $$\left\{ a_{n} \right\}$$ , we may ask whether the terms $$a_{n}$$ of the sequence approach some specific number $$L$$ as $$n$$ gets larger and larger. If they do, we say that the sequence $$a_{n}$$ converges to $$L$$ .

note.title: Limit of a Sequence
note.paragraph: Let $$\left\{ a_{n} \right\}$$ be a sequence. We say that the sequence $$\left\{ a_{n} \right\}$$ converges and has the limit $$L$$ , written
if the terms of the sequence, $$a_{n}$$ , can be made as close to $$L$$ as we please by taking $$n$$ sufficiently large. If a sequence is not convergent, it is said to be divergent .
